description: The baseline brief: a plain exposure breakdown must produce a market-value panel grouped by sector, and nothing that fails validation.
brief: Where is our equity exposure concentrated by sector?
notes: Catches a planner that answers a breakdown question with a holding count or an unrelated grouping.

description: A brief naming one fund must actually restrict a panel to that portfolio -- not report firm-wide numbers under the fund's name.
brief: Give me a climate risk overview of the Sustainable Leaders Fund
notes: The single most consequential planning error in this domain: the right number for the wrong book.

description: A brief about change over time must produce a trend panel, not a single point-in-time snapshot.
brief: How has our exposure moved across the snapshots we have?
notes: Catches a planner that answers 'how has it moved' with today's figure.

description: A brief asking for two dimensions at once should cross-tab them rather than emit two separate one-dimensional panels.
brief: Show me sector exposure broken out across every portfolio in a single grid
notes: House expectation: 'in one view' means a pivot; two stacked breakdowns do not answer it.

description: A data-coverage brief must aggregate the actual data-point field, since coverage and excluded market value are only computed for weighted_avg_datapoint panels.
brief: Where is our climate data thin -- which parts of the book have no emissions figures?
notes: Catches a planner that describes coverage in a title instead of planning the query that measures it.

description: A brief with no resolvable subject must come back as a clarification with no panels invented.
notes: The refusal case. A plausible-looking dashboard built on a guessed interpretation is worse than no dashboard.

description: A brief about data this system does not hold must be refused rather than mapped onto the nearest available dimension.
brief: What is our exposure to companies with a female CEO?
notes: Catches the failure mode where an unavailable attribute gets silently substituted with country or sector.
